canonical_title: A Dark-Haired Girl & PKD: Letters from the Heart, the Spleen, and the Funnybone
author: Philip K. Dick; Linda Levy; compiled by Linda Castellani
card_summary: Compiled by Linda Castellani in 2008, this correspondence gathers PKD's letters to Linda Levy, the young woman he pursued in the mid-1970s, ranging across affection, complaint, and the manic humor he aimed at people he wanted to charm.
page_summary:
This document assembles the letters Philip K. Dick wrote to Linda Levy, one of the several dark-haired women who moved through his Orange County years and his fiction alike. The letters run by turns tender, aggrieved, and clowning, exactly as the compiler's subtitle promises: the heart, the spleen, and the funnybone were the three registers PKD reached for whenever he was courting someone.

The correspondence dates from the same stretch that produced the Selected Letters of 1975-1976, when PKD was living in Fullerton, recovering from 2-3-74, and writing to a wide circle of friends, scholars, and would-be lovers. Levy belongs to the private half of that circle, and the letters show the domestic, flirtatious, and self-dramatizing PKD who rarely surfaces in the more scholarly correspondence.

As an archived compilation the item preserves letters that fall outside the published Underwood-Miller volumes, making it useful for tracing how PKD wrote to individuals rather than for the record.
